questions.question: In a family, both parents have brown eyes, but their child has blue eyes. A geneticist explains that eye colour is determined by dominant and recessive alleles. According to you the blue eye colour allele is:
questions.solution: (b) Recessive. Both brown-eyed parents are heterozygous carriers; the trait hidden in them appears in the child only in the homozygous recessive condition.

questions.question: Delhi experienced heavy smog during winter. People complained of difficulty in breathing, burning eyes, and reduced visibility. Doctors advised children and elderly people to stay indoors. The reduced visibility during smog is caused by:
questions.solution: (a) Suspended particulate matter. Fine suspended particles (with fog) scatter light and reduce visibility.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Thrombin converts fibrinogen to fibrin.
Reason (R): Calcium ions are necessary for thrombin to function.

options.c: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.d: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution: (a) (A) is true and (R) is false.. Thrombin does convert soluble fibrinogen into insoluble fibrin. Calcium ions are needed (with thrombokinase) for converting prothrombin INTO thrombin, not for thrombin's own action, so R as stated is incorrect. (Some keys may accept (d) if R is read loosely as 'calcium is needed for thrombin formation'.)

questions.question: India's population crossed 1 billion in the year 2000 and continues to grow. The government promotes small family norms and awareness about family planning methods. Still in some regions the birth rate remains high. One major reason for high birth rate in certain regions is:

options.d: Lack of awareness about family planning

questions.solution: (d) Lack of awareness about family planning. Illiteracy and lack of awareness about contraception keep birth rates high.

questions.question: The diagram given below shows a black shaded region known as corpus callosum. The function is to ____:

options.c: Transfer information from one cerebral hemisphere to the other
options.d: Transfer information from one cerebellum hemisphere to the other

questions.solution: (c) Transfer information from one cerebral hemisphere to the other. The corpus callosum is a band of nerve fibres connecting the two cerebral hemispheres.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): There is less urination in winter than in summer.
Reason (R): In summer, sweating is more, so less water is given out in the form of urine.

options.c: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.d: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution: (b) (A) is false and (R) is true.. Urination is MORE in winter (little sweating, so excess water leaves as urine); hence A is false. R is true: heavy sweating in summer reduces urine volume.

questions.question: During an accident, Aman felt a sudden rush of energy. His heartbeat increased, breathing became faster, and he felt more alert. This is due to the release of:
questions.solution: (a) Adrenaline. Adrenaline (fight-or-flight hormone from adrenal medulla) raises heart rate, breathing rate and alertness.

questions.question: Cutting the tip of a plant allows lateral buds to grow because:
questions.solution: (d) Auxin concentration decreases. Auxin from the apical bud suppresses lateral buds (apical dominance); removing the tip lowers auxin so lateral buds grow.

questions.question: During day time, a large tree loses a significant amount of water through its leaves by the process of transpiration. This water loss is necessary to:

options.d: Cool the plant and transport nutrients.

questions.solution: (d) Cool the plant and transport nutrients.. Transpiration cools the leaves and creates the pull that carries water and minerals up the plant.

questions.question: The small differences in traits among individuals of the same species are called:
questions.solution: (b) Variation. Differences among individuals of a species are variations.

questions.chapter: Cell Cycle and Structure of Chromosomes
questions.topic: Cell cycle phases at root tip
concepts: Cell cycle phases at root tip
questions.question: A young root tip is examined under the microscope. Cells near the tip show active division with visible chromosomes. Cells farther away from the tip are larger but not dividing instead show active growth. The actively dividing region at the root tip corresponds to which phase of the cell cycle?
questions.solution: (c) M - Phase. Visible chromosomes and active division occur in the M (mitotic) phase.

questions.question:
Veera tried to match the parts of an eye with its correct explanation as given in the table below:
P - Optic nerve : The nerve which leaves the eye ball
Q - Sclera : The white portion of the eye ball
R - Retina : It is sensitive to light consisting of the rods and cones
S - Choroid : It is richly supplied with blood vessels for providing nourishment to the eye
Identify the correct sequence:
questions.solution: (a) P, Q, R, S. Every part is already matched correctly with its explanation, in the order P, Q, R, S.

questions.question: Arnav sat to study for his exam but was unable to focus as there was too much noise around him. He felt disturbed and wished for a quiet place to learn. Every time he tried to read a page, the noise distracted him and he had to start again. Arnav felt frustrated because he wanted to prepare well for his exam but the noisy environment would not let him focus. Associate yourself with Arnav's plight and identify how would this impact you.

options.a: Interrupts concentration, disturbs peace of mind, stress
options.b: Stress, difficulty in remembering information, increases concentration
options.c: Difficulty in remembering information, increases efficiency of work, stress
options.d: Increases efficiency of work, disturbs peace of mind, interrupts concentration

questions.solution: (a) Interrupts concentration, disturbs peace of mind, stress. Noise reduces concentration and causes mental disturbance and stress; it never increases concentration or efficiency.

questions.question: The pigment chlorophyll is a highly complex substance composed of carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen and:
questions.solution: (b) Magnesium. Magnesium is the central atom of the chlorophyll molecule.

questions.question: The movement of ovum takes place across the female reproductive system in a specific pathway. Identify the correct sequence of its movement.
questions.solution: (d) Ovary, Ovum, Fallopian tube, Uterus. The ovum is released from the ovary, enters the Fallopian tube and then reaches the uterus.

questions.question:
Given below is the diagram of a Nephron. Read the information below and fill in the blanks:
Nephron is a structural and functional unit of a kidney. The production of urine occurs here in three major steps. It cleanses our blood by removing waste and extra water, while retaining the things our body needs. The clean blood is circulated back into our body, and the waste becomes urine.
The process of ultrafiltration takes place in the (a) ______ (Bowman's capsule / Glomerulus) of the nephron. The fluid formed as a result is called (b) ______ (glomerular filtrate / Urine) which enters into the (c) ______ (Distal convoluted tubule / Proximal convoluted tubule). The fluid after reabsorption and (d) ______ (Tubular secretion / Micturition) enters into the (e) ______ (Malpighian capsule / Collecting duct).
questions.solution: Glomerulus

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: Explain the term Mortality.
questions.solution: Mortality (death rate) is the number of deaths per 1000 individuals of a population per year.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: In what form are the substances secreted during nervous and hormonal coordination respectively.
questions.solution: Nervous coordination: neurotransmitters (chemical messengers, e.g. acetylcholine) released at synapses, with the message carried as electrical impulses. Hormonal coordination: hormones secreted directly into the blood by endocrine glands.

Aaryan is performing an experiment in the school laboratory. In spite of keeping all the chemicals around, he has forgotten one important chemical to be used.
(a) Which part of the brain will help Aryan to remember and recollect the chemical needed?
(b) Name the part of brain that helps him coordinate his movements while handling the fragile glass apparatus while performing the experiment.
questions.solution: (a) Cerebrum (seat of memory, intelligence and reasoning). (b) Cerebellum (coordinates and balances voluntary muscular movements).

concepts: Sites of light and dark reactions
questions.question: State the location where the light and dark phase of photosynthesis take place.
questions.solution: Light phase (photochemical): in the grana (thylakoids) of the chloroplast. Dark phase (biosynthetic / Calvin cycle): in the stroma of the chloroplast.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: What is Mutation?
questions.solution: A mutation is a sudden heritable change in the genetic material (gene or chromosome) of an organism.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: Differentiate between Geotropism and Chemotropism with reference to the stimulus associated with each movement.
questions.solution: Geotropism: growth movement of a plant part in response to gravity (stimulus = gravity). Chemotropism: growth movement in response to a chemical (stimulus = chemicals, e.g. growth of pollen tube towards ovule).

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: Give the technical term for the contraction and the expansion phase of the heart respectively.
questions.solution: Contraction phase: Systole. Expansion (relaxation) phase: Diastole.

questions.question: Name the two natural resources under pressure due to population explosion.
questions.solution: Any two: land/forests, water (fresh water), food, fossil fuels/energy, minerals. E.g. water and land (forests).

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
A woman from a rural, mountainous region visits a clinic with a visibly swollen neck. Her diet mostly consists of rice and vegetables grown locally. She rarely eats seafood or salt. She complains of fatigue and difficulty concentrating.
(a) Identify the above condition.
(b) Name the hormone associated with this problem.
(c) Give the cause of such a symptom.
questions.solution: (a) Simple (endemic) goitre. (b) Thyroxine (thyroid hormone). (c) Deficiency of iodine in the diet (no iodised salt/seafood) - the thyroid cannot make enough thyroxine, so TSH stimulates the gland to enlarge, causing the swollen neck.

marking_points.point: (c) Iodine deficiency in diet causing thyroid enlargement

questions.solution: Semen is the milky fluid ejaculated by the male, consisting of sperms suspended in secretions of the seminal vesicles, prostate gland and Cowper's glands.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Mr. Shyam and his friend add excess fertilizer to the small plants growing in their garden. Without any knowledge about gardening, they thought more fertilizer would let the plant grow faster.
(a) Which type of solution will the soil become with the use of excessive fertilizer?
(b) What will be the state of the roots in the soil as mentioned in (a)?
(c) How can the roots be brought back to normal state from the condition mentioned in (b)?
questions.solution: (a) Hypertonic solution. (b) Water leaves root cells by exosmosis, the cells become plasmolysed (flaccid) and the plant wilts. (c) By watering the soil heavily (making it hypotonic) so water re-enters cells by endosmosis - deplasmolysis.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: State Mendel's law of dominance.
questions.solution: When two homozygous individuals with contrasting characters are crossed, only one character (dominant) expresses itself in the F1 generation while the other (recessive) remains hidden.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
State the rate of photosynthesis in plants when there is:
(a) Rise in temperature.
(b) Reduced absorption of water from the soil.
questions.solution: (a) Rate increases with rise in temperature up to an optimum (about 25-35 °C); beyond that it falls as enzymes are denatured. (b) Rate decreases - water shortage causes stomata to close (less CO2 entry) and less water for photolysis.

marking_points.point: (a) increases up to optimum then decreases

questions.question: Which blood vessel supplies oxygenated blood to the walls of the heart? Where is this blood vessel arising from?
questions.solution: Coronary artery; it arises from the base of the aorta (aortic arch just above the left ventricle).

questions.question:
Shreeja finds difficulty in observing the school board from a distance as she sits on the last bench. She visits an ophthalmologist. She understands everything the doctor explains because she has learned those concepts in class. The doctor suggests she wear suitable spectacles to correct her defect. (Diagram shows parallel rays passing through a concave lens before the eye and focusing on the retina.)
(a) What defect she is suffering from?
(b) Which type of lens is used to correct the defect mentioned in (a)?
(c) What could be one of the reasons for such a defect?
questions.solution: (a) Myopia (short-sightedness). (b) Concave (diverging) lens. (c) Eyeball elongated (too long from front to back) or lens too convex/thick, so image forms in front of the retina.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: Explain the term Double circulation.
questions.solution: Blood passes through the heart twice in one complete cycle - once through the pulmonary circuit (heart-lungs-heart) and once through the systemic circuit (heart-body-heart).

marking_points.point: Blood passes twice through heart: pulmonary + systemic

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: Distinguish between ovary and testis based on the processes occurring within it.
questions.solution: Ovary: oogenesis - produces ova (and secretes oestrogen/progesterone). Testis: spermatogenesis - produces sperms (and secretes testosterone).

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
A region is facing increasing desertification. Local farmers notice that native plants like cacti and acacia survive while other crops fail. They are planning to plant trees to prevent soil erosion and improve the ecosystem.
(a) State the characteristic adaptation in cacti to survive.
(b) What is the purpose of such modification?
questions.solution: (a) Leaves are modified into spines (and the stem is green, fleshy and has a thick cuticle with sunken stomata). (b) To reduce the surface area for transpiration and thus conserve water (stem stores water and carries out photosynthesis).

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: Mention the parts of the neuron present in the gray matter and the white matter of the cerebrum.
questions.solution: Grey matter (outer cortex of cerebrum): cell bodies (cytons) and dendrites of neurons. White matter (inner): myelinated axons (nerve fibres).

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: Draw a neat labelled diagram of a human sperm cell.
questions.solution: Draw a sperm with head, middle piece and tail. Labels: acrosome (at tip), nucleus (in head), neck/centrioles, middle piece with mitochondria (spiral), tail.

marking_points.point: Correct diagram with head, middle piece, tail

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: How does the hormonal method of contraception work?
questions.solution: Oral contraceptive pills (synthetic oestrogen and progesterone) inhibit ovulation (block FSH/LH release), so no ovum is released and fertilisation cannot occur.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: Mention two body features of Homo Habilis.
questions.solution: Any two: cranial capacity about 650-800 cc; height about 1.2-1.5 m (short); erect posture and bipedal; jaws and teeth smaller than earlier forms; hands capable of making stone tools.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: Colour blindness is more common in men than in women. Explain Why?
questions.solution: Colour blindness is caused by a recessive gene on the X chromosome. Men (XY) have only one X, so a single defective allele makes them colour blind. Women (XX) need the recessive allele on both X chromosomes; with one normal X they are only carriers.

marking_points.point: Male has one X so one allele expresses; female needs two (carrier otherwise)

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: Insulin is injected into the body of a highly diabetic patient and it is not given orally. Give a suitable reason.
questions.solution: Insulin is a protein hormone; if taken orally it would be digested by proteolytic enzymes (pepsin, trypsin) in the alimentary canal and become ineffective. Injection delivers it directly into the blood.

marking_points.point: Would be digested by enzymes if taken orally

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Kunal is a football player. He injured his lower back in a game. When the doctor taps his patellar tendon, he quickly moves his leg in response.
(a) Name this process.
(b) What is the pathway of the above process?
(c) Which parts of the central nervous system is responsible for such an action?
questions.solution: (a) Knee-jerk reflex (a simple spinal reflex action). (b) Reflex arc: Receptor (in tendon/muscle) -> Sensory neuron -> Spinal cord (relay/interneuron) -> Motor neuron -> Effector (thigh muscle, which contracts and jerks the leg). (c) Spinal cord.
